For the decay  

π⁺  →  μ⁺  +  ν  

take c = 1.  The pion is at rest, so its total energy is just its rest-mass energy  

Eπ  =  mπ  = 139.6 MeV .

Let  

Eμ , pμ   be the energy and momentum of the muon,  
Eν , pν   be the energy and momentum of the (essentially mass-less) neutrino.

1. Energy conservation  
   Eμ + Eν = 139.6 MeV .                       …(1)

2. Momentum conservation (back-to-back particles)  
   pμ = pν  ≡ p .                              …(2)

3. Dispersion relations  
   μ⁺ (mass mμ = 105.7 MeV):   Eμ² = p² + mμ² ,  
   ν  (m ≈ 0):                   Eν = p .

Using (2) and substituting p = Eν into the muon relation:  

Eμ² – Eν² = mμ² .                              …(3)

From (1):  Eμ = 139.6 – Eν .  Insert this in (3):

(139.6 – Eν)² – Eν² = (105.7)²  
⇒ 139.6² – 2·139.6·Eν = 105.7²  
⇒ Eν = (139.6² – 105.7²) / (2·139.6) .

Compute:

139.6² = 19488.16  
105.7² = 11172.49  

Eν = (19488.16 – 11172.49) / 279.2 ≈ 29.8 MeV .

Therefore  

• Neutrino kinetic energy (all its energy):  Kν ≈ 29.8 MeV.  

• Muon total energy:  Eμ = 139.6 – 29.8 ≈ 109.8 MeV,  
  so its kinetic energy is  
  Kμ = Eμ – mμ ≈ 109.8 – 105.7 ≈ 4.1 MeV.

So the kinetic energies are approximately 4.1 MeV (μ⁺) and 29.8 MeV (ν).

Answer: A
